lessons.title: Meet the Guitar — First Clean Sounds
goals: Sit so your shoulders can stay loose
Name the open strings low to high: E A D G B E
Get all six open strings to ring without buzz
lessons.theoryBite: Thick to thin, standard tuning is E A D G B E. Saying the names out loud while you pluck trains your ear for free.
drills: Get comfortable: guitar on your leg, fretting thumb behind the neck
Pluck open strings low to high and say each name
Hold each open string about two seconds — if it dies early, pluck again softer and cleaner
lessons.masteryCheck: Name and pluck all six open strings in order without peeking at the headstock.

privateLesson.hook: Day one: make noise that feels good. No wrong notes yet.
privateLesson.teacherIntro: Hey — welcome. Today isn’t about being “good.” Hold the guitar so your hands can relax, learn the string names, and hear six clear open notes. That’s a real first win.

guide.example: Leave your fretting hand off the strings. Pluck the thickest string and say “E.” Let it ring for two counts. Continue A, D, G, B, E toward the thinnest string. Repeat once without looking at the names.
guide.listen: Six separate, ringing notes. The last E sounds higher than the first. Keep your picking hand clear of the string after each pluck.
guide.rescue: Work on just the thickest three strings: E, A, D. If a note stops abruptly, check that neither hand is touching the vibrating string.

steps.title: Find the thickest string
steps.instruction: Rest the guitar comfortably. Leave the hand that presses the strings off the neck. Pluck the thickest string once. Its name is low E.

steps.title: Name the six strings
steps.instruction: Move from the thickest string to the thinnest: E, A, D, G, B, E. Pluck one string at a time and say its name.

steps.title: Let each note ring
steps.instruction: Pluck each string again. Count “1, 2” before moving to the next. Keep both hands clear of the string while it rings.

steps.title: Try without looking
steps.instruction: Look away from the string names. Say each name as you pluck from thickest to thinnest. If you forget, check the names and try again.

terms.meaning: The metal wires across the neck mark the frets. Fret 1 is nearest the tuning pegs. Press the string just before the wire, on the side nearer the pegs.
A string you play without pressing it against a fret.
String 1 is the thinnest E. String 6 is the thickest E. Thickest to thinnest: 6 E, 5 A, 4 D, 3 G, 2 B, 1 E.
The hand that presses the strings against the neck. Your other hand picks or strums.

lessons.title: Fretting Hand — Just Enough Pressure
goals: Fret with fingertips, right behind the metal fret
Use the lightest press that still sounds clean
Play frets 1–4 on the high E evenly
lessons.theoryBite: One fret is one half-step. Press just behind the fret wire — middle of the box makes you squeeze harder for a worse sound.
drills: Slow spider 1-2-3-4 on the high E around 50 BPM — stop and fix buzz before you add speed
Buzz-then-add: ease off until it buzzes, then add a hair of pressure
Quick mirror check — curved knuckles, wrist not collapsed
lessons.masteryCheck: Play frets 1–4 on the high E evenly at 60 BPM with clear tone.

privateLesson.hook: Day two — pressure without panic.

guide.example: On the thinnest E string, put your index finger just behind fret 1, on the nut side of the wire. Pick once. Repeat at fret 2 with the middle finger, 3 with the ring finger, and 4 with the little finger. Start without a click, then try one note per beat at 50 BPM.
guide.listen: Four clear notes rising in pitch, with equal gaps. Use only enough pressure to stop the buzz; release the pressure between attempts.
guide.rescue: Use just frets 1 and 2. Move closer to the fret wire before adding pressure. Make the reach smaller and rest if the hand feels strained.

steps.title: Place one fingertip
steps.instruction: Use the thinnest E string. Place your index fingertip just before the first metal fret wire, on the side nearer the tuning pegs. Pick the string once.

steps.title: Find a light touch
steps.instruction: Slowly ease the pressure until the note buzzes. Add just enough pressure to make it clear again. Keep the fingertip close to the fret wire.

steps.title: Add the other fingers
steps.instruction: Play fret 1 with index, fret 2 with middle, fret 3 with ring, and fret 4 with little finger. Play one note at a time on the same string.

steps.title: Give the notes equal time
steps.instruction: Repeat 1–2–3–4 slowly with equal gaps. When that feels comfortable, use a metronome at 50 beats per minute, one note per click. Work toward the 60 BPM target later.

Beats per minute: the speed of the pulse. At 60 BPM, a metronome clicks once each second. Play one note per click unless the exercise says otherwise.

lessons.title: First Chord Win — E Minor
goals: Build open Em with two fingers
Strum all six strings on the beat
Lift Em off and put it back ten times cleanly
lessons.theoryBite: E minor is the notes E G B. Open Em: middle finger on A string fret 2, ring on D string fret 2. Easiest full-sounding chord — we start here on purpose.
drills: Build Em, count to four, release — do that ten times
Down-strums on beats 1 and 3 only — name what you hear on the clean reps
String audit: pluck each string alone and fix anything dead
lessons.masteryCheck: Hold Em for eight steady down-strums with every string ringing.

privateLesson.hook: First real chord: Em — two fingers, instant band energy.
privateLesson.teacherIntro: Em is the friendliest full chord on the guitar. Two fingers, all six strings. We’ll build it slow, check every string, then strum like a song already started.

guide.example: Place your middle finger on string 5 (A), fret 2, and ring finger on string 4 (D), fret 2. Leave the other strings open. Pick all six separately, then strum downward on counts 1 and 3 while counting “1, 2, 3, 4.”
guide.listen: Every string rings, including the open G next to your ring finger. Two bars give you four evenly spaced strums.
guide.rescue: If the G is muted, curve your ring finger so its side clears that string. Recheck just A, D, and G before strumming again.

steps.title: Place the first finger
steps.instruction: Put your middle fingertip on the A string, fret 2. The A string is the second-thickest string.

steps.title: Place the second finger
steps.instruction: Put your ring fingertip on the D string, fret 2. D is the next string toward the floor. Leave the other four strings open: do not press them.

steps.title: Check one string at a time
steps.instruction: Pick all six strings, thickest to thinnest. If one is silent or buzzy, adjust the nearby fingertip and pick that string again.

steps.title: Play eight slow strums
steps.instruction: Count “1, 2, 3, 4” slowly. Brush down across all six strings on 1 and 3. Repeat the count four times for eight strums. This chord is E minor, written Em.

steps.title: Keep the music going

guide.listen: The downstrokes stay on the numbers. The two upstrokes fit halfway between beats, without making the next downstroke late.
guide.rescue: Leave out the chord. Use muted strings and play only downstrokes on 1, 2, 3, 4. Add just the upstroke after 4, then the one after 2.
guide.example: Count “1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and” evenly. The numbers are the main beats; “and” is halfway between them. Lightly touch the strings with your fretting hand so they do not ring. Strum down on each number and move up on each “and.” Keep that hand motion. Touch the strings on 1, 2, the “and” after 2, 3, 4, and the “and” after 4. Pass above the strings on the “and” after 1 and 3. Hold G and play the same pattern. Repeat “1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and” eight times. Each full count is one bar. Slow down if you lose the count.

steps.title: Move the strumming hand
steps.instruction: Lightly touch the strings with your fretting hand so they do not ring. Strum down on each number and move up on each “and.”

steps.title: Leave two upstrokes silent
steps.instruction: Keep that hand motion. Touch the strings on 1, 2, the “and” after 2, 3, 4, and the “and” after 4. Pass above the strings on the “and” after 1 and 3.

steps.title: Add a G chord
steps.instruction: Hold G and play the same pattern. Repeat “1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and” eight times. Each full count is one bar. Slow down if you lose the count.

goals: Find the A root for box 1 on the low E string at fret 5
Walk the box up and down slowly with a pulse

lessons.theoryBite: After a week of chords, five notes are enough for first lead. A minor pentatonic is A C D E G. Box 1 (root on low-E fret 5) is the common rock/blues map — fewer notes means more room for rhythm and space, which is how solos start sounding like music.

guide.example: Play the thickest E string open and the A string at fret 2. Sound only those two strings. This is E5, a power chord. Place index on low E fret 3 and ring on A fret 5. Pick only those two strings together. Lightly touch unused strings to keep them quiet. Slide both fingers two frets toward the guitar body: index to low E fret 5, ring to A fret 7. Keep the same two-string shape. Count four beats per bar. Play G5 once per beat for two bars, then A5 once per beat for two bars. Repeat the whole pattern twice at a comfortable speed.

goals: Roll the barre finger for even light pressure

terms.meaning: The metal wires across the neck mark the frets. Fret 1 is nearest the tuning pegs. Press the string just before the wire, on the side nearer the pegs.

The hand that presses the strings against the neck. Your other hand picks or strums.
Brush across several strings in one motion. A downstroke moves from thicker strings toward thinner strings.

A group of beats. In 4/4, count 1, 2, 3, 4; that is one bar. Other time signatures group beats differently.
A string is kept from ringing, usually by touching it lightly. Muting can be intentional; a finger accidentally touching the next string can also silence it.

goals: Treat silence as a rhythmic event you can aim

lessons.title: Dynamic Waves — Crescendo Strum (3)
goals: Use dynamics inside a single riff
Accent the riff's peak note
Keep the groove under the volume changes
lessons.theoryBite: A riff is more than notes — it's where you push and where you pull. Accents give it a spine. If the foot rushes, the hands will too; rebuild from quarters.
drills: Play the riff at one flat volume, 4 bars — foot stays on quarters the whole time
Same riff, accent the peak note louder — if you rush, drop back to downstrokes only
Then swell the whole riff over 4 bars — count out loud for one cycle, then whisper
Return to flat and hear the difference — foot stays on quarters the whole time
lessons.masteryCheck: The same riff with accent and swell, groove intact the whole time.

privateLesson.hook: If it feels good at 70 BPM, you’re winning. Crescendo Strum (3).
privateLesson.teacherIntro: About 30 minutes together. Warm up, learn one clear thing, then play something that feels like music. First win: Use dynamics inside a single riff.

goals: Turn the odd accent into a hook
Make the 5-beat pattern recognizable on its own

lessons.title: Comp Patterns — Two Rights, One Left (4)
goals: Build a comp pattern that works in a full band
Match the drummer's backbeat
Leave the bass frequencies to the bassist
lessons.theoryBite: In a band, comp is a slot, not a solo. Play the rhythmic pocket and get out of the bass's way. If the foot rushes, the hands will too; rebuild from quarters.
drills: Comp muted eighths with the backbeat — foot stays on quarters the whole time
Drop the low E string from the pattern — if you rush, drop back to downstrokes only
Play only beats 2 and 4 for 8 bars — count out loud for one cycle, then whisper
Then the full pattern, locked to the drum feel — foot stays on quarters the whole time
lessons.masteryCheck: A band-ready comp that locks to the backbeat and stays out of the bass register.

privateLesson.hook: Groove is a superpower. Speed is optional; pocket is not. Two Rights, One Left (4).

lessons.title: Question Harmony — Solo Over Andalusian (2)
goals: Use Phrygian color over the E
Make the E bar feel dark, then released
Keep the F bar bright in contrast
lessons.theoryBite: Phrygian's flat 2 makes E feel dark and tense. The F chord is the bright window in the dark room. Leave space; one clear target note beats a blur of almosts.
drills: Play E Phrygian phrases on the E bar only — end the phrase on a chord tone when you can
Switch to F-major-ish lines on the F bar — half volume on the answer phrase
Contrast the two colors across two passes — silence counts as part of the lick
End each pass on E and let it ring — no nervous extra notes
lessons.masteryCheck: Two-bar color contrast: dark Phrygian on E, bright on F, resolving each time.

terms.meaning: The metal wires across the neck mark the frets. Fret 1 is nearest the tuning pegs. Press the string just before the wire, on the side nearer the pegs.
A string you play without pressing it against a fret.
String 1 is the thinnest E. String 6 is the thickest E. Thickest to thinnest: 6 E, 5 A, 4 D, 3 G, 2 B, 1 E.
The hand that presses the strings against the neck. Your other hand picks or strums.
Brush across several strings in one motion. A downstroke moves from thicker strings toward thinner strings.
Beats per minute: the speed of the pulse. At 60 BPM, a metronome clicks once each second. Play one note per click unless the exercise says otherwise.
A string is kept from ringing, usually by touching it lightly. Muting can be intentional; a finger accidentally touching the next string can also silence it.

lessons.title: Year Capstone — Full Path Performance
goals: Warm up with something easy that sounds like you
Run a mini-set (two or three pieces/sections) with planned order
Recover from at least one intentional flub without stopping the show
lessons.theoryBite: Year capstone: show a path, not perfection. Warm up kindly, run a short set with recovery skills, and leave knowing what you own. Mastery is repeatable music under light pressure — not a flawless fantasy take.
drills: Light warm-up: open strings or easiest song section for three minutes
Full run of your set once with notes allowed, once with fewer notes
Dress-rehearsal energy: stand if you can, breathe before downbeats, smile after the last chord
lessons.masteryCheck: Complete a short set you would play for a friend, with recovery and a clear ending.

terms.meaning: A string you play without pressing it against a fret.
String 1 is the thinnest E. String 6 is the thickest E. Thickest to thinnest: 6 E, 5 A, 4 D, 3 G, 2 B, 1 E.
Brush across several strings in one motion. A downstroke moves from thicker strings toward thinner strings.
A group of beats. In 4/4, count 1, 2, 3, 4; that is one bar. Other time signatures group beats differently.

spec.title: Open strings (standard)
spec.caption: Low E through high e in standard tuning.

notes: Standard tuning low→high: E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4
String numbers in tab: 6 = low E, 1 = high e
